title: Differential Diagnosis and Case Formulation
description: Evaluate clinical case descriptions to distinguish Major Depressive Disorder with anxiety from Bipolar II.
problemStatement:
A 28-year-old software engineer presents with severe exhaustion, anhedonia, and feelings of worthlessness for the past 3 weeks. However, collateral history from their spouse reveals that 4 months ago, the patient went 5 consecutive days without sleeping, launched 3 separate businesses simultaneously, spoke at lightning speed, and maxed out their credit cards on luxury watches.

### Requirements:
1. Provide the precise DSM-5 differential diagnosis (distinguishing between Unipolar Major Depressive Disorder and Bipolar Disorder).
2. Explain why prescribing an SSRI antidepressant alone without a mood stabilizer poses severe danger for this patient (risk of triggering mania).
3. Outline the evidence-based biopsychosocial treatment protocol (pharmacotherapy + psychoeducation + CBT).
hints: Hint 1: The presence of a past manic or hypomanic episode rules out unipolar depression and confirms a Bipolar diagnosis.
Hint 2: Antidepressant monotherapy in bipolar patients can induce rapid mood switching into severe mania.
